minutes.headline: Committee backed a resolution against spring MCAS, passed school choice at five seats each for grades 9 and 10, and required post-travel testing.
minutes.summary: The School Committee met remotely and handled a long run of routine action items: a line item transfer, student custodian hours, donations, a full-return MOA, travel testing, a Galapagos trip, and class funds. It drafted a resolution against 2021 MCAS testing, heard a summer program overview, and decided not to pursue a single-district virtual school. School choice seats were set, two policies were approved on third read, and achieve program credits were approved.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer, electricity to maintenance of building contract
budget_items.what_was_said: Money moves to fund roof repairs at the primary school and building design work for Turkey Hill, while leaving enough in electricity.
Extra Monday and Friday hours will be paid from a COVID prevention entitlement grant, with no local budget impact. The student custodians get no extra benefits.

budget_items.topic: PTO donations to Turkey Hill gift account
budget_items.what_was_said: Three PTO checks were presented for teacher appreciation, general use and art supplies.
Staff will be credited back sick time used to get vaccinated, and the benefit is to be extended to all employee groups.
The approved budget already holds money for the summer program. The bridge program is not in the budget and would be grant funded. Next summer is expected to use a federal relief grant (SR2).
The FY22 budget cannot fund a new school, and ESSER money would have to be absorbed into the local budget later.
Families who leave the trip get a refund less a fee, or a voucher they can sell for full value.

budget_items.topic: Special Olympics fundraising by student groups
budget_items.what_was_said: Student groups raised money for Special Olympics.
Capital planning will recommend raising the capital project threshold, and the first twelve ranked projects go to town meeting.

transfers.description: From the electricity line to the maintenance of building contract line, for primary school roof repairs and Turkey Hill building design

decisions.decision: The committee will draft a revised MASC MCAS resolution within about 48 hours, sign it electronically, and send it to legislators and senators.
No committee member objected to the superintendent's recommendation not to pursue a single district virtual school.
The committee asked for an update on the summer program at the later August meeting.
Capital planning will bring a recommendation to raise the capital project threshold to FinCom.

what_happened.line: The School Committee passed the edited MASC resolution on MCAS and high stakes testing by roll call, with all yes votes heard.
The committee accepted school choice numbers as presented: five seats in grade nine and five in grade ten.
The committee voted to keep requiring testing after out-of-state travel over 24 hours for the rest of the school year.
A transfer from electricity to the maintenance of building contract passed; the minutes tie it to primary school roof repairs and Turkey Hill design work.
The committee noted no objection to the superintendent's advice not to pursue a single-district virtual school, and approved the full-return MOA.

why_it_matters: The school choice seat limits set the number of out-of-town students the district can enroll in grades 9 and 10, which touches school enrollment and the money that follows students.

The virtual school discussion noted the FY22 budget cannot fund a new school and that federal relief money would later have to be absorbed into the local budget, which would bear on future tax-supported school spending.
The student custodian hours are paid from a COVID prevention grant, so no local budget impact was stated for that item.
watch_next: An update on the summer program, requested at the later August meeting.
A capital planning recommendation to FinCom to raise the capital project threshold, with the first twelve ranked projects going to town meeting.
